s1.syndrome_frame: Postpartum breast symptoms with erythema and discharge
salient_findings: Excessive milk expression despite weaning attempts
Milky, nonpurulent discharge from both breasts
key_facts: Three prior episodes of similar symptoms
Normal hormone levels during first trimester of pregnancy
No recurrent headaches or visual changes
5 cm × 8 cm area of erythema and induration on the medial aspect of the right breast
Anaerobic culture positive for Streptococcus agalactiae

raw.syndrome_frame: Postpartum breast symptoms with erythema and discharge
salient_findings: Excessive milk expression despite weaning attempts
Milky, nonpurulent discharge from both breasts
key_facts: Three prior episodes of similar symptoms
Normal hormone levels during first trimester of pregnancy
No recurrent headaches or visual changes
5 cm × 8 cm area of erythema and induration on the medial aspect of the right breast
Anaerobic culture positive for Streptococcus agalactiae

shortlist.label: Puerperal mastitis
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum presentation with breast erythema and discharge, elevated leukocyte count, and positive anaerobic culture for Streptococcus agalactiae

shortlist.label: Mastitis due to Streptococcus agalactiae
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anaerobic culture for Streptococcus agalactiae and clinical presentation of mastitis

shortlist.label: Prolactinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated prolactin levels and previous treatment with cabergoline, a dopamine agonist used to treat prolactinomas

shortlist.label: Hyperprolactinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated prolactin levels and clinical presentation of galactorrhea and amenorrhea

shortlist.label: Lactational mastitis
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum presentation with breast erythema and discharge, and history of excessive milk expression

raw.rationale: The patient is 11 weeks postpartum, presenting with breast erythema and pain, and has been experiencing excessive milk production, which are all consistent with lactational mastitis. The presence of a milky, nonpurulent discharge and the absence of fluctuance or a focal lesion on ultrasound also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Puerperal mastitis
rejected.why: While puerperal mastitis is a consideration, the term typically refers to mastitis occurring in the first few weeks postpartum, and the patient's presentation at 11 weeks postpartum, along with the specific details of her case, makes lactational mastitis a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mastitis due to Streptococcus agalactiae
rejected.why: Although the anaerobic culture was positive for Streptococcus agalactiae, the clinical presentation and other findings are more indicative of lactational mastitis, which can be caused by various factors, including infection.

rejected.label: Prolactinoma
rejected.why: The patient's elevated prolactin level and previous treatment with cabergoline suggest a history of hyperprolactinemia, but the current presentation is more consistent with lactational mastitis than a prolactinoma, especially given the absence of headaches, visual changes, or a discrete pituitary lesion on MRI.

rejected.label: Hyperprolactinemia
rejected.why: While the patient has an elevated prolactin level, the primary issue at hand is the breast symptoms, which are better explained by lactational mastitis than by hyperprolactinemia alone.

rejected.label: Mastitis
rejected.why: This option is too broad and does not specify the type of mastitis. Given the patient's postpartum status and symptoms, lactational mastitis is a more specific and appropriate diagnosis.
